sections.title: Positioning
sections.summary: Klaviyo has repositioned from email marketing to an 'autonomous B2C CRM' led by two AI agents. Older product pages still sell email on ROI, so the story is mid-transition.
keyPoints: Homepage: 'THE AUTONOMOUS B2C CRM', led by Composer, an AI marketing agent that you approve step by step.
The enterprise page repeats the CRM frame; the Email product page still leads with 'Email marketing that delivers wins—and 63x avg ROI'.
Scale claim repeated across pages: 200,000+ brands in 100 countries.

sections.title: Products and offerings
sections.summary: Two AI agents sit on one data platform, with classic channels and customer tools underneath.

rows: AI marketing agent that plans calendars, builds campaigns and audits flows, with human approval
AI customer service that resolves questions and recommends products
Campaigns and flows with predicted-value personalization
Included in plans for a set number of profiles
Product reviews, limited by orders per month on lower plans

gaps: Flows, segmentation, forms and RCS pages were in the navigation but not opened.

sections.title: Pricing
sections.summary: A free plan, a $20 Email plan and a recommended Marketing plan priced by active profiles, with a custom lane for the largest senders. AI and service products come as small free allowances, then as add-ons.
keyPoints: Billing unit: active profiles, meaning contacts you can reach; unsubscribed and suppressed contacts do not count.
Marketing plan promo: $1 for the first month, for up to 5,000 active profiles, marked limited time.
Everything above 250 free profiles is chosen with a profile slider, so higher prices sit behind an interaction.

rows: 250 active profiles, 500 emails a month, $10 of Composer usage, 10 Customer Agent resolutions
500 active profiles, 5,000 emails a month, plus the free-plan allowances
Everything in Email, plus social marketing, reviews with no order limit and Customer Hub
Over 150,000 active profiles, volume pricing, data warehouse sync, enterprise security

gaps: Prices above the first profile tier were not captured.
SMS and Composer add-on prices were not shown.

sections.title: Merchandising
sections.summary: A free plan with a sample of every new product is the most generous entry offer of the three. The weakness is how much of the price list sits behind a slider.
keyPoints: The Marketing plan carries a 'recommended' badge, a $1 first month and a comparison table.
A tab switches the pricing page between plans and all products; AI and service products appear as add-ons.
Product pages pair 'Sign up' with 'View pricing'.
For merchants: personalization from purchase history and predicted value, product recommendations inside service conversations, and cart recovery.
Not shown: catalogue, collections or search tooling. Klaviyo works on messages and data, not the storefront.

sections.title: Technical platform
sections.summary: A public developer site with an API reference, SDKs for server and mobile languages, a CLI, an MCP server and an agent-ready docs index. Enterprise copy stresses custom objects, 400+ integrations and warehouse sync.
keyPoints: API reference covers every endpoint with parameters, request and response bodies and an example request.
SDKs: Python, PHP, Ruby and Node on the server; iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter on mobile.
Agent connection options: docs, an OpenAPI spec, an MCP server and a CLI. The docs publish a machine-readable page index (llms.txt).
Enterprise page: works with your warehouse, CDP and models rather than replacing them; custom objects, APIs and 400+ integrations.
gaps: Rate limits and webhook behaviour were not read.

sections.title: Design
sections.summary: Recognizable and built around real product UI in device frames, with a palette that does not look like a template. It is assembled from separate pieces: marketing, docs and signup each use a different typeface.
keyPoints: Home uses a custom typeface (Klaviyo Degular); the docs headline uses Geist Pixel Square and the signup page uses Instrument Sans.
Palette: white and black with an orange-red band (#ff4b33) and a lime accent (#deff00); a lime promo bar sits above the navigation.
Button corners are 2px on the home page and 12px in the docs.
The Composer page switches to a dark theme with a chat-style product mockup; the pricing page is short, 4,436px tall.
Merchant design control (email and form templates) was not shown in the surveyed pages.
gaps: Email and form design tools were not surveyed.

sections.title: Company presentation
sections.summary: The newsroom shows a company in expansion, and customer proof is outcome-led with named brands.
keyPoints: Recent news: a headless platform opened to agents, an AI-agents launch, a Google partnership and new regional headquarters.
A new Chief Product Officer was appointed following the acquisition of an agency team and technology.
Customer proof: Thirdlove reports 15x SMS ROI, and Dermalogica describes Klaviyo as its CRM and CDP.
Brand-count claim: 200,000+ brands, repeated on several pages.
gaps: No About page surfaced; the newsroom was the company page.

jtbd_fit.evidence: Pages for service, abandoned cart recovery and email each name a specific job; home names two agents for two jobs.

capability_visible.evidence: Free plan makes the product tryable; Composer prompt library and product tours are public. Product UI itself is behind signup.

pricing_transparency.evidence: Free, $20 and $25 plans plus a separate page explaining the billing unit. Higher profile tiers are behind a slider and add-ons are not priced.

product_breadth.evidence: Two agents plus channels, flows, reviews, helpdesk and a customer hub; the CRM label stretches across products whose pages still sell email.

platform_depth.evidence: Public API reference, seven SDK languages, CLI, MCP server and an llms.txt index; custom objects and 400+ integrations for enterprise.

time_to_value.evidence: Capture stops at the signup form.

friction.evidence: One click from home. First screen asks only for an email or Google; password and store details come later.

trust.evidence: Named brands with outcomes (Thirdlove, Dermalogica) plus analyst mentions. Brand-count appears on several pages.

mobile.evidence: Phone captures exist for home and pricing but were not assessed.

states.evidence: No error or empty states reached.

value_prop_clarity.evidence: 'Autonomous B2C CRM' and 'AI marketing agent' are category language; the subhead explains the job.

proof_quality.evidence: Customer outcomes are named, but '63x avg ROI' and '65% resolved autonomously' have no method on the page.

persuasion_integrity.evidence: The $1 first-month offer states its cap and that it is limited time.

cta_logic.evidence: 'Sign up' plus 'View pricing' appear together on product pages; enterprise swaps in 'Talk to sales'.

company_narrative.evidence: Homepage says AI agents and CRM; the Email page still sells email ROI. Newsroom supports the agent story.

offer_packaging.evidence: Free, Email, Marketing and Custom are clearly separated with a comparison table and a recommended badge. Most prices sit behind a slider.

offer_architecture.evidence: Free plan with small allowances of every product, a $1 first month, add-ons for AI and service, and a custom lane above 150,000 profiles.

merchant_merch_tools.evidence: Personalisation, product recommendations in messages and cart recovery are shown; there are no catalogue, collections or search tools.

visual_craft.evidence: A distinctive palette and real product UI in device frames. The lime bar, orange band and white sections compete on the home page.

system_coherence.evidence: Three typefaces across home, docs and signup; button corners of 2px on home and 12px on docs; dark Composer page next to white pages.

merchant_design_control.evidence: The surveyed pages did not show email or form design tools.

read.summary: A company mid-reposition: the homepage and newsroom sell autonomous AI agents on a CRM, while product pages and the pricing grid still read as an email platform. Platform openness and a real free plan are the strongest parts.
pros: A free plan with allowances for every new product lets a merchant try the whole stack.
Developer site is open: API reference, SDKs, CLI, MCP server, llms.txt.
Signup starts with only an email or Google.
Promo pricing states its cap and duration.
cons: The CRM and agent story is not carried onto the Email product page, which leads with ROI.
'63x avg ROI' and '65% resolved' have no method shown.
Prices beyond the first profile tier require using a slider.
read.howItSells: Sells autonomy with oversight: AI agents that do the work while the marketer approves. Supports it with a free tier, named brand outcomes and an open developer platform.
copy: Include small allowances of every new product in the free plan.
State the cap and end of a promo price.
avoid: A new category name on the homepage while product pages use the old one.
Headline ROI numbers with no method.
unknowns: Add-on prices for SMS, Composer and Customer Agent.

hypothesis.statement: Rewriting the Email product page headline to match the agent-led homepage ('Your AI marketing agent runs your email') will keep visitors on one story and lift page-to-signup rate.
hypothesis.guardrail: Organic search entry traffic to the page
hypothesis.decisionRule: Ship if signup-start rises by a pre-agreed margin and organic entries do not fall in a four-week split.

merchandising.summary: A free plan with a sample of every product is the most generous entry offer of the three. The weakness is how much of the price list is behind a slider.
pros: Free plan allowances introduce every new product.
The Marketing plan is marked recommended and has a $1 first month.
Product pages carry a pricing link next to signup.
cons: Prices above the first tier require using a slider.

design.summary: Recognisable and showing real product, but built from separate pieces: a different typeface on home, docs and signup, and dark and white sections that don't share a rule.
pros: Real product UI in device frames on the home and Composer pages.
A palette that does not look like a template.
Pricing page is short and scannable.
cons: Three typefaces across home, docs and signup.
Different button corner radii between home and docs.
Promo bar, orange band and white sections compete.

claims.text: Customer Agent resolves 65% of questions autonomously.
Email marketing that delivers wins—and 63x avg ROI
Thirdlove drives 15x SMS ROI after consolidating email and SMS in Klaviyo
Limited time: Get your first month of an eligible Klaviyo Marketing Plan for just $1, for up to 5,000 active profiles.

signupPath: 'Sign up' goes to klaviyo.com/sign-up, a short page with 'Continue with Google' or an email box and a 'Continue with email' button. Only an email address is asked on this page. What follows was not reached.
